summary.text: A four-year-old girl with no notable pathological history presented to the emergency department with acute left flank abdominal pain and non-bloody vomiting. Examination showed an apyretic patient in good general condition with a distended abdomen, a left flank mass and pelvic tenderness.

Ultrasound with color Doppler showed a large cystic mass and a twisted vascularized pedicle with a whirlpool sign suggesting left adnexal torsion, and CT showed a cystic left flank mass with fatty and calcified components and a twisted pedicle. Serum AFP and beta-hCG were negative.

Pfannenstiel laparotomy found a large solid left ovarian mass with a twisted fallopian tube, no perforation and no adhesions, and a left adnexectomy was performed for torsion and non-viability of the adnexa. The resected mass had a smooth external surface and contained hair and sebaceous material, and histology was consistent with a mature teratoma of the left ovary.
The postoperative course was uneventful, the patient was discharged on postoperative day 2, and a follow-up ultrasound at one month was normal.
